To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rats prefer to choose a large reward that is delivered in three successive trials (a bundle) over a smaller reward delivered immediately (single) when the larger reward is 150 microl sucrose solution and the smaller reward varies between 25 and 150 microl across trials.
rats show increased preference for delayed over immediate rewards when they are presented in bundles.
impulsive choice in rats was reduced when a reward was chosen in a series of three trials (bundled), as compared with when it was chosen once and delivered after the choice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model that will predict the choice of a larger, delayed reward (LL) over a smaller, immediate reward (SS) in rats.
the neural mechanisms of self-control, which is the capacity to resist temptations and to delay gratification.
the neural mechanisms of decision-making and the role of the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) in the control of impulsive behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study demonstrates that bundling of rewards can increase tolerance for delay.
the present results demonstrate that bundling of rewards is an effective strategy for reducing impulsive choice.
the results presented here suggest that the ability to bundle rewards in time can be a building block of self-controlled behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ability to control one's behavior is not innate, and that it can be learned by the process of bundling.
the tendency to choose the larger-later over the smaller-sooner reward can be enhanced by the perception that one is making a series of consistent choices.
the perception of predictability can increase tolerance for delay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bundling can reduce the discounting of delayed rewards.
bundling is a simple and robust way to increase the tolerance for delay.
impulsive choice is a function not only of the amount of reward but also the number of choices that an organism has to make in order to receive the reward.
